title: Requiring a reported depth error raised the ComCat shallow-share change by 19.15 points in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested how depth-error selection changes a time comparison in 12,848 global ComCat earthquakes at preferred M >=5.5. Between 2000-2012 and 2013-2025, the reported depth <=15 km share rose by 12.68 percentage points. Requiring a finite reported depth error gave a 31.84-point rise. The extra rise was 19.15 points, with conditional 95% two-year block limits of 16.07 to 22.30 points. Error values were absent for 82.99% of early records and 3.27% of later records. An exact decomposition separates field-availability selection from further selection by an error limit. A 5 km cut gave a 30.86-point rise: 12.68 plus 19.15 from availability selection minus 0.98 from the further cut. A 2 km cut gave an uncertain 4.47-point decline and retained only 82 early events. Removing three depth labels reduced the availability effect. Later-era comparisons gave much smaller selection differences. This is an exploratory catalog audit, not evidence of physical shallowing or calibrated depth errors. Revised records, source mix, short selected samples and untested depth accuracy limit inference. Original code, aggregate counts, paired uncertainty draws, source hashes, a figure and a separate count audit are included. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Left: annual depth-error missingness and 5 km cut retention. Right: selected late-minus-early depth <=15 km share changes, with conditional 95% two-year block intervals. Selection changes the time comparison; the figure does not estimate physical depth changes.

citations.reason: Same global source, eras and shallow cutoff; we add depth-error availability and error-limit selection, not a repeat of spike deletion.
Local error-cut failure motivates a global time-comparison audit and an availability decomposition.
Depth-measure disagreement motivates caution about physical interpretation.
Prior regional bounds limit physical interpretation; our outcome is metadata selection.
Prior median sensitivity bounds provide context; no prior analysis code reused.
